title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
data_curation: Pretraining data covers web, code, STEM, multilingual text and images (knowledge cutoff 2026-01-04), filtered with heuristics and quality classifiers, aggressively deduplicated and decontaminated against benchmarks. Agentic SFT data comes from a synthetic pipeline modelled on Agents Research Environments. Personas are sampled from demographics and Big Five traits, or grounded in real text, and each gets a 'universe' of 10-14 contacts with weeks of email, calendar and WhatsApp history plus mock CLI and GitHub tools that return real-format JSON. Scenarios with verifiable rubrics are generated on top. Post-processing drops failed, duplicate and fourth-wall-breaking trajectories, loss-masks bad tool calls, and removes hallucinated or false-success traces via grounding judges. Teacher rollouts from Muse Spark RL/RLHF runs are kept when above a reward threshold, with later checkpoints preferred, and are stripped of grader metadata and teacher-identity references. Privacy (Contextual Integrity) and safety traces are prompt-distilled from Muse Spark and rejection-sampled.
curriculum: Pretraining is logit co-distillation from Muse Spark's top-256 logits, using only a KL loss for the first 95% of training and only CE for the final 5% to correct top-k truncation bias. The final checkpoint is uniformly averaged with three earlier checkpoints spaced 600 steps apart. Mid-training Phase 1 (domain infusion) adds synthetic reasoning traces at a reduced LR. Phase 2 (agentic) extends context from 32K to 128K, adds tool-use and agent trajectories, and switches to CE because teacher logits are less reliable on that data. Post-training then runs SFT (about one epoch per dataset), on-policy distillation from Muse Spark (which consistently gives better downstream RL than going straight from SFT to RL), and multi-objective RL over reward models, verifiers, task success and RLHF.
method: A dense 29.6B causal Transformer chosen over MoE: scaling ladders at a fixed 32GB memory budget showed dense to be 2-2.5x more compute-efficient. It has 52 layers, hidden size 6656, GQA with 32 query and 2 KV heads, a 3-local:1-global attention pattern with a 2048-token sliding window, RoPE (theta 500K) on local layers only, gated attention, SwiGLU (19,968), the 202K Llama 4 tokenizer and 128K+ context. A frozen 1.8B Perception Encoder (ViT-G/14) handles images. A simplified MLA variant was tried and underperformed GQA on RULER. Reasoning strength (low, medium, high, xhigh) is trained during RL by splitting each prompt's samples into subgroups with different length penalties, and some prompts are routed only to high strengths. Privacy RL penalizes oversharing. Safety RL deterministically penalizes executing attacker-seeded actions and rewards recognizing untrusted content. Messages are routed with to= recipients and tool calls use the XML ATEM format. Deployment uses EvoPress mixed Q4/5/6_K quantization (19.65GB) for 32GB devices, Q4KM for 24GB devices, and a 5-layer DFlash drafter with block size 16.
eval_metrics: Agentic and coding: tau3-Banking, WildClawBench, GAIA2, GDPval-AA, SciCode, OSWorld-Verified, SWE-Bench Verified/Pro (bash plus file tool, 4 runs), TauBench and Terminal-Bench 2.1. Tool use: MCPAtlas and PinchBench. Reasoning: DeepSearchQA, AIME 2026, GPQA-D, ARC-AGI and HLE. Also IFBench, SkillsBench, multimodal benchmarks (CharXiv, MMMU-Pro, OmniDocBench, ScreenSpot), BEAM-128K, AA-LCR, privacy and security (CIMemories, PrivacyLens, Siren AgentDojo) and multilingual (Omnilingual-GAIA2, MMLU-ProX, FLoRes+). Results at high reasoning: SWE-Bench Verified 76.0, SWE-Bench Pro 51.2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 51.7, MCPAtlas 75.5, GAIA2 43.3, AIME26 94.7, GPQA-D 83.5, IFBench 77.0, AA-LCR 80.0, Omnilingual-GAIA2 60.4. For quantization, average accuracy over 15 tasks is 75.7 (BF16), 75.6 (EvoPress) and 74.8 (Q4KM).
key_results: At high reasoning, Muse Glimmer beats Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on MCPAtlas (75.5 vs 54.2/62.5), SWE-Bench Pro (51.2 vs 36.9/50.2), AA-LCR (80.0 vs 68.3/73.3) and Omnilingual-GAIA2 (60.4 vs 37.5/45.0). It trails Qwen3.6-27B on OSWorld-Verified (65.9 vs 75.6), Terminal-Bench 2.1 (51.7 vs 60.7) and GDPval-AA. EvoPress 4-bit-class quantization keeps 75.6 of the BF16 model's 75.7 average accuracy.
evolution_note: Meta's on-device follow-up to Llama 4 (it shares that tokenizer) distills the frontier Muse Spark model, combining logit co-distillation in pretraining with Qwen3-style on-policy distillation before RL. Unlike Gemma 4 and Qwen3.6, it argues for a dense model over MoE under a hard 32GB memory budget. It builds privacy (Contextual Integrity) and prompt-injection robustness into training for local agents such as OpenClaw. The report gives no RL algorithm details, reward formulas or post-training data sizes.
